evals.prompt: Send an order confirmation with UniOne from our Node.js backend to the customer.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Node.js SDK or email/send with the key from the environment, sets idempotence_key, reads failed_emails.
expectations: Reads the key from an environment variable
Does not call the API from the browser

evals.prompt: We send the same newsletter text to 300 users with UniOne; make it fast.
evals.expected_output: One email/send with up to 500 recipients and per-recipient substitutions, not 300 calls.
expectations: Does not invent a batch endpoint

evals.prompt: Add a webhook endpoint that marks UniOne bounces in our database (Python).
evals.expected_output: webhook/set, checks the MD5 auth over the raw body, answers 200 fast, handles hard_bounced.

evals.prompt: I have no domain yet — how do I try UniOne?
evals.expected_output: The sandbox flow: get-sandbox-domain, confirmed-email/create, send to the confirmed address.
expectations: Mentions confirmed emails and the 48-hour link
Does not suggest fake test addresses
